description: [S7.6, kind `scope`] The app wires S7.2's focus-child callback (U-1616) to LiveSession::focus_child_takes, which answers 0 for every key: at HEAD c6d7d78b no window of the port's tree takes keys before the root (showCharacterEditor's bio arm throws MissingResource{"showCharacterEditor: the bio EditBox"}, chareditor.cpp), so every key reaches the root handlers 7 / 8 / 9. The live core also counts a command 12 / 13 as a violation (no HANDLER record carries it, live.cpp) and writes no MSG records for it.
path to resolution: After S1 merges (its bio EditBox and parse_trace's focus keys, U-1604), answer the callback from the port's focus state on the sim thread's side (a flag the editor sets while its EditBox has the focus) and record 12 / 13 as MSG 0x100 / 0x102 with no HANDLER after them.

description: [S7.6, kind `scope`] Two cursor sources: `--cursor system` (default) answers the game's cursor reads with GetCursorPos + ScreenToClient through the window's viewport (the original's Display::getCursor), `--cursor message` with the last mouse message's point (lParam through the same viewport). The tests use `message`, because app_drive.py posts WM_MOUSEMOVE without moving the system cursor; a session in `system` mode with a real mouse is recorded the same way (every answer is in the trace), but no test drives the system cursor (moving it would take the desktop's mouse) and the two sources differ whenever the cursor is outside the client or between two mouse messages.
path to resolution: A recorded play session with the real mouse (S7.5's playtest), replayed with sg_run_boot (the recording carries the answers, so it replays either way) and its hover frames checked.

description: [S7.6, kind `value`] Idle passes of an unpaced modal loop run when the cursor moved (at most one per `--pass-ms`, default 10) and every `--idle-ms` (default 200) while nothing happens; the original runs its menu passes continuously, each with a waitTicks(1, 0) (10 ms) the port drops (tick_menu.inc hover loop). A loop whose drawing follows its pass count runs slower than the original: courseActionMenu's location-screen blink alternates every 8 recording positions in the measured session (presents.tsv of log/roadmap/S7/6_probe runs), i.e. every 8 idle passes = 1.6 s at 200 ms. Title-menu idle CPU measured over 10 s: 0.00 % with --idle-ms 0, 1.72 % with 500, 3.27 / 3.59 % with 200 (one idle pass of the title menu costs about 6.5 ms of CPU).
path to resolution: S7.5's playtest decides the rate (or a pass clock at the original's 10 ms for the loops that draw by pass count, with the CPU measured again); a drawing-only pass could skip the present when the back buffer is unchanged before the gfx dump (needs a gfx.h accessor, S2's file).

description: [S7.6, kind `scope`] The host never dispatches a press and its release in one pump call: a dispatch ends before a release (onPress1 1, onPress2 4, onChar0 9) whose press (onPoint 2, onPoint2 5, onChar 8) is in it, as S7.1's script host chunks a click or a key. Measured need: with app_drive.py's back-to-back WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_LBUTTONUP in one dispatch the location screen dropped the Monterey click (probe session 2, 0 frames after it), split it entered the course in every later session. What the original does with a press and release that reach one PeekMessage loop (a very fast real click) is not measured.
path to resolution: One recording of the original with a down / up pair posted together (S7.4's game slot), reading which pass of courseActionMenu sees the press.

description: [S7.6, kind `scope`] The port drops waitTicks (tick.cpp kDrops: `wait loop (pacing)`), so the live app does not hold the game where the original waits inside a frame or a menu: waitTicks(0x5a, ebp) ML+0xecfc (900 ms) and waitTicks(0xa, ebp) ML+0xf6da (100 ms) in tick_frame.inc, waitTicks(0x3c, 0) in tick_menu.inc (600 ms). Only H1's frame wait is paced (LiveHost::wait_point). An interruptible waitTicks returns 1 on input in the original; the port's drop returns 0 and dispatches nothing, and the live host does the same, so the recording still replays.
path to resolution: A LiveIo hook at the waitTicks drop (tick.cpp TkBase::call, a shared-file change) through which the host sleeps n * 10 ms; the return value stays the drop's.

description: [S7.6, kind `value`] Frame pacing under load: with the sim thread at normal priority and the PC at 100 % CPU (12 logical processors busy with other processes) a gate run measured 354 frame periods with median 95 ms and only 75.7 % within 87 + 10 + 2 ms (max 295); the frames' own work is 3..10 ms (waits.tsv), so the excess was the sleeping thread waking late. With THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL on the sim thread (host.cpp LiveSession::run) and the same load: 355 periods 87..100 ms, median 93, 99.7 % within 99 ms; bit 17: 58 periods 125..135, median 128. The priority changes no recorded value. Not measured: in-game drawing load (S7.5), and whether the priority starves the window thread on a single-core machine.
path to resolution: S7.5 measures in-game load; a playtest on another PC.

description: [S7.6, kind `scope`] A modal loop that pumps twice at one cursor count (no cursor read between its pumps, measured in cov_a_keys: 1 inflated dispatch) gets one idle pass and then must_deliver: the host waits for input there, so such a loop's time-driven passes between inputs (showHoleStatsScreen's clock-read page turns, U-1601) do not run in a live session. The inflated dispatch's CURSOR record sits in front of the dispatch while the read it stands for comes later, so a gfx.snapshotAt position between the two is taken one item late in a replay.
path to resolution: Tell the core the loop (InputSource::batch has no caller argument; commands.cpp pump_messages has `where`), so that loops known to read no cursor could be paced by their clock reads instead.

description: [S7.6, kind `scope`] A session the window stops inside a modal loop (the title menu) has no FRAME record: its recording replays (sg_run_boot runs the boot frame over the whole trace), but no record is compared, and the replay's last passes come from TraceInput's tail-idle rule, not from the live session's (U-1605 / U-1606). Every gated session here ends at a frame head after >= 30 frames.
path to resolution: Cut a mid-pump stop back to the last recorded item, or end title-only sessions at the next frame head.

description: [S7.6, kind `value`] Presents of a paced modal loop happen at every pass the host allows (one per --pass-ms while nothing is queued); the CPU of a paced wait (pumpAndRedraw: narrateShot's SimFoto, the '.' / '/' waits) was not measured in the app.
path to resolution: Measure a paced wait in the app (the modal_wait script's keys through app_drive.py) and rate-limit its presents if the CPU calls for it.

description: [S7.6, kind `scope`] The present check compares sgh64 of the back buffer on the sim thread (presents.tsv), of the presenter's frame on the window thread (shown.tsv) and of the replay's gfx.snapshotAt copies, and the client pixels only at quiescent points (the title menu and the three hover frames, captured through the window DC as S7.3 does). A frame shown for less than the capture's latency (in-game frames) is judged by the hashes alone, not by its pixels on screen.
path to resolution: A capture taken at each present's WM_PAINT (a window-thread hook in window.cpp, S7.3's file) or PrintWindow on a timer in the driver.
